summary: Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. She held a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She held posts at UC Berkeley (attested 2008), UCLA (attested 2016), and the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Natasha Reichle is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Joanna Gottfried Williams, alongside teachers Amin Sweeney, Lewis R. Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between approximately 2011 and 2018 under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker.

Nathan Sivin was a Sinologist and historian educated at DLI, MIT, Harvard, and Kyoto University. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977, was Professor Emeritus at the University of Pennsylvania (1977-2006), and was Honorary Professor at CAS (~2014-2022).

Nathan W. Hill specializes in Tibetology, linguistics, and computational studies. After studying at Harvard (~2001-2009) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff, he held positions at SOAS, UC Berkeley, Oxford, and Trinity College Dublin.

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indologist and linguist who was educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford (1768). He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and studied with traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Grove specializes in Tibetology and computational fields. He held affiliations at the University of Virginia, where he is attested in 2006 and as a Research Associate in 2026.

Nathaniel Tarn was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Cambridge, Paris, and Chicago. He taught at LSE, SOAS (~1963-1967), Princeton (1970), and served as a professor at Rutgers University from 1972 to 1985.

Nathmal Tatia was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee, studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982-1990).

Navalpakkam Ramanuja Tatacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry and served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University from 1989 to 1994.
Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a Lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi under Mamluk Ali Nanautawi between approximately 1845 and 1853.
Neal Donner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).
Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and Indology, attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Wilfried Swenden.

Nenghai Shi was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Peking University and under Kecheng Zhang, Foyuan, Guanyi, and Khangsar Rinpoche. He founded the Shaocheng Society of Buddhist Studies (1917) and was vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953-1966).
Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
